title: The NEET-UG 2024 Paper Leak Case
dek: India's medical entrance exam for 2.4 million aspirants was compromised by a leak traced to a stolen question-paper trunk in Hazaribagh, Jharkhand. The CBI has filed multiple chargesheets, but the Supreme Court refused to order a national retest.

heroStat.label: NEET-UG 2024 candidates whose results the Supreme Court refused to cancel nationwide, despite confirmed leak-related arrests in Bihar and Jharkhand

promise.quote: The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test will be conducted securely and fairly, on the basis of a question paper whose integrity is fully protected until the moment of the exam.

target.description: An exam conducted for over 2.4 million candidates on the basis of a question paper that remained sealed and uncirculated until the scheduled test time, assessed strictly on merit.
target.standard: NTA's own examination-security protocols for a national-level competitive entrance exam.

reality.description: An FIR was filed at Shastri Nagar police station in Patna on 5 May 2024 — the day of the exam — alleging that an organised gang had shared the question paper and answer key with several students the night before. Investigators traced the leak to a trunk of question papers stolen in Hazaribagh, Jharkhand. Bihar's Economic Offences Unit formed a SIT, and the CBI took over the investigation on 24 June 2024. The CBI arrested Oasis School (Hazaribagh) principal Ahsanul Haque and vice-principal Imteyaz Alam on 28 June 2024, and four AIIMS Patna MBBS students accused of solving leaked papers for a fee on 18 July 2024. The CBI filed its first chargesheet against 13 accused on 2 August 2024, naming alleged masterminds Sikander Yadvendu and Manish Prakash; a second chargesheet against six more accused followed on 20 September 2024; and a fifth supplementary chargesheet was filed on 22 November 2024. Separately, the Supreme Court on 23 July 2024 declined to order a nationwide retest, holding there was no evidence the leak was 'systemic' enough to vitiate the entire exam for 2.4 million candidates, and on 22 October 2024 dismissed a review petition against that ruling. A retest was offered only to 1,563 candidates who had been given contested grace marks; those marks were separately cancelled.

verdict.summary: This is a stub entry, pending fuller research. The leak itself — a stolen question-paper trunk and organised distribution network centred on Patna and Hazaribagh — is well documented through multiple CBI chargesheets. But the Supreme Court explicitly declined to find the leak 'systemic' enough to affect the national result, so the two central facts of this case — a confirmed criminal conspiracy, and a national exam result the courts let stand — sit uneasily next to each other. Both are reported here without resolving that tension further.
verdict.reasoning: The FIR, arrests, and multiple chargesheet dates are corroborated across government press releases (newsonair.gov.in, drawing on PIB/CBI statements) and multiple independent outlets. However, this entry has not traced the case beyond the fifth supplementary chargesheet (November 2024), has not confirmed any trial verdicts, and has not independently reviewed the Supreme Court's full judgment text.
